families.native: Claude makes it with no third-party account: the output is code, rendered by Claude or by a free local tool.
families.connector: Claude calls a hosted service through an MCP connector. The service generates or edits and bills its own credits.
families.api: Claude Code writes the call to a model's API. You hold the key and pay per second of output.
families.app: No integration with Claude is established. Claude writes the shot brief and you run it in the app.
families.local: Open-weight models you run yourself, on your own GPU or a rented one.
families.pipeline: Open-source end-to-end kits that chain script, voice, footage, captions and render.
families.distribution: Getting the finished file onto a channel. Every publish is a human decision.

evidenceLevels.documented: Read on the provider's own page on checkedOn.
evidenceLevels.third-party: Reported by a third-party guide or tracker; not confirmed on the provider's page.
evidenceLevels.unverified: The provider's page could not be read on checkedOn; listed from the provider's homepage or reputation.
evidenceLevels.tested: Run end to end by a maintainer; the test is linked in notes.

routes.name: Claude Motion
routes.howFromClaude: In claude.ai, ask for a Motion animation, edit it in chat or in the editor, then Export > MP4.
routes.access: Beta on Team and Enterprise plans. On by default for Team; Enterprise owners turn it on under Organization settings > Artifacts.
routes.cost: Counts against the plan's usage limits; longer animations use more.
routes.notes: Built as code from the Motion template, so a word or a number can change without regenerating the rest. Resolution and maximum length are not published.

routes.name: Artifacts: animated HTML pages
routes.howFromClaude: Ask for an HTML artifact animated with CSS or GSAP. Render it to MP4 with HyperFrames, or capture it with a screen recorder.
routes.access: Free, Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise all include artifacts.
routes.notes: The page is the source and the video is a render of it. The route for anyone without Team or Enterprise.

routes.name: Claude Code + HyperFrames
routes.howFromClaude: npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes, then /hyperframes to compose and /hyperframes-cli to lint, preview and render.
routes.access: Free, Apache-2.0, runs locally.
routes.notes: Plain HTML is the easiest format for an agent to write. In zhuyansen/awesome-claude-video-skills' test of 16 skills, it took 23.5 minutes on a 15-second brief, the slowest.

routes.name: Claude Code + Remotion
routes.howFromClaude: Install remotion-dev/skills, scaffold with npx create-video@latest, render with npx remotion render or on Remotion Lambda.
routes.access: Free for individuals and for-profit companies with up to 3 employees; larger for-profits need a Remotion company licence.
routes.cost: Local render, or AWS Lambda per render.
routes.notes: React components with props, so one template renders many personalised versions. Licence: remotion-dev/remotion LICENSE.md.

routes.name: Claude Code + Manim or Motion Canvas
routes.howFromClaude: Ask Claude Code for a Manim scene in Python or a Motion Canvas scene in TypeScript and render it locally.
routes.access: Free, MIT.
routes.notes: Manim Community is the maintained fork of 3b1b/manim. Motion Canvas: github.com/motion-canvas/motion-canvas.

routes.name: Claude Code + FFmpeg, auto-editor, WhisperX
routes.howFromClaude: Point Claude Code at the files. WhisperX transcribes with word timings, auto-editor removes silences, FFmpeg trims, reframes and burns captions.
routes.access: Free and local.
routes.notes: Cutting and captioning only. For transcript-based editing in an app use Descript; for dubbing use ElevenLabs. Kits that wrap this route: nateherkai/herk-edit-kit, pireel/pireel (AGPL-3.0).

routes.name: Product demo from the running app
routes.howFromClaude: Claude in Chrome records short browser flows; latent-spaces/brag turns a finished project into a launch video in one command.
routes.access: Claude in Chrome needs a paid plan (Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise). brag is MIT.
routes.notes: Real UI earns more trust than generated UI. Record first, then add titles in code.

routes.name: Higgsfield MCP
routes.howFromClaude: Add the connector at mcp.higgsfield.ai and approve it once; Claude picks a model and submits each generation.
routes.access: Higgsfield account. Higgsfield's own post lists Veo 3.1, Kling 3.0, Seedance 2.0, Wan and MiniMax Hailuo, up to 4K and about 15 seconds per clip.
routes.cost: Higgsfield credits, billed separately from Claude.
routes.notes: One connector reaching many frontier models. The model list is Higgsfield's own claim; it may lag model shutdowns such as Veo 3.1 on the Gemini API.

routes.name: HeyGen MCP (avatars) and HyperFrames hosted MCP
routes.howFromClaude: Avatar videos through the HeyGen connector. The hosted HyperFrames MCP composes and renders from claude.ai; from Claude Code its compose and render tools are disabled, so use the local skill.
routes.access: HeyGen account; check the current plan limits on HeyGen's pricing page.
routes.notes: Any avatar of a real person needs that person's consent.

routes.name: ElevenLabs MCP (hosted)
routes.howFromClaude: Add ElevenLabs from the Claude connectors directory and sign in with OAuth. No server to run.
routes.access: ElevenLabs account.
routes.notes: The audio layer for every other route: voiceover, translated dubs that keep the speaker's voice, music and effects. The older local repo elevenlabs/elevenlabs-mcp is archived; use the hosted connector.

routes.name: Descript MCP and API
routes.howFromClaude: Connect the Descript MCP and ask for imports and edits. Exports of media files are manual in Descript for now.
routes.access: Any paid Descript plan.
routes.cost: Draws on the plan's AI credits and media minutes.
routes.notes: The route when the edit is about what people said. The API exports transcripts, timelines and share links, not media files.

routes.name: OpenArt MCP
routes.howFromClaude: Connect OpenArt, list models with their cost, upload references through the picker, then generate.
routes.access: OpenArt account.
routes.cost: OpenArt credits; generations you cannot afford are refused.
routes.notes: Useful when the job starts from a still you already like.

routes.name: vidIQ MCP
routes.howFromClaude: Connect vidIQ. Its tools cover research (outliers, keywords), generation (video, b-roll, clips, voiceover, music) and publishing (YouTube upload, Instagram reels).
routes.access: vidIQ account; a YouTube or Instagram connection for publishing.
routes.notes: The one connector here that covers research, generation and upload. Every upload or publish is a human approval.

routes.name: Canva MCP
routes.howFromClaude: Import a Claude Motion animation by URL, apply a brand kit, resize to each format, export.
routes.access: Canva account.
routes.notes: A last step when a brand kit and many aspect ratios matter more than custom motion.

routes.name: Figma MCP (motion and video export)
routes.howFromClaude: Read motion context from a Figma file, author motion with Figma's motion skill, export video.
routes.access: Figma account with the MCP server enabled. Motion and export may need a paid seat; check Figma's plan page.
routes.notes: The guide documents the MCP server; motion authoring and video export are inferred from the server's tool list (get_motion_context, export_video) seen on 2026-10-20, not from a Figma help page.

routes.name: Runway MCP plugin
routes.howFromClaude: Install the plugin from runwayml/runway-mcp-plugin and add a Runway API key.
routes.access: Runway API key.
routes.notes: Published under the runwayml organisation, but young. Read its README before relying on it.

routes.name: ComfyUI MCP
routes.howFromClaude: Run ComfyUI, connect an MCP server such as artokun/comfyui-mcp, and let Claude queue workflows.
routes.access: A ComfyUI instance on a capable GPU.
routes.notes: Brings the local family into chat. Alternative: ATH-MaaS/Pixelle-MCP.

routes.name: Gemini Omni Flash via the Gemini API
routes.howFromClaude: Claude Code calls the Interactions API (client.interactions.create, model gemini-omni-1.1-flash). Output arrives inline as base64 by default; for files over 4 MB request delivery 'uri', then poll files.get until state is ACTIVE and download.
routes.access: Google AI Studio key on the paid tier.
routes.cost: About $0.10 per second of 720p output; 1080p and 4K bill higher. Google's pricing page, read 2026-10-20.
routes.notes: Google's recommended successor to Veo 3.1 on the Gemini API. 360p to 4K (1080p and 4K are upscaled), 16:9 or 9:16; extensions add 3 to 10 s up to 40 s total. gemini-omni-flash-preview shuts down on 2026-10-22. Price: ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing.

routes.name: Veo 3.1
routes.howFromClaude: Do not start a new Gemini API integration on Veo 3.1. Use gemini-omni-api, or the GA Veo models on Google's Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.
routes.access: Gemini API IDs veo-3.1-generate-preview, veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview and veo-3.1-lite-generate-preview shut down on 2026-10-22.
routes.cost: Until shutdown: $0.40/s at 720p and 1080p, $0.60/s at 4K; Fast $0.10 to $0.30/s; Lite $0.05 to $0.08/s.
routes.notes: Listed because most Veo tutorials online still use these IDs. Google's Veo 3.1 prompting guide still teaches the shot structure well.

routes.name: Grok Imagine video (xAI API)
routes.howFromClaude: Claude Code calls the xAI API with grok-imagine-video-1.5 (native 1080p) or grok-imagine-video (720p, supports edit and extend).
routes.access: xAI API key.
routes.cost: Not listed on the capability page; see xAI's models page.
routes.notes: Clips run 1 to 15 seconds. Only the 720p model edits a source clip (up to 8.7 s) or extends one by 2 to 10 s.

routes.name: Kling, Seedance, Runway and Luma APIs (pointer)
routes.howFromClaude: Pick the model in the comparison list below, then have Claude Code write the client from that provider's API docs.
routes.access: An account and key per provider, or one aggregator key.
routes.cost: Per second or per clip, changing monthly.
routes.notes: Not yet split into one row per provider. Anil-matcha/awesome-ai-video-models keeps the priced comparison; it is maintained by an aggregator vendor.

routes.name: Sora (OpenAI)
routes.howFromClaude: Do not build on it.
routes.access: None. The app closed on 2026-04-26 and the Videos API and Sora 2 endpoints were retired on 2026-09-24.
routes.notes: Listed so nobody follows an old Sora tutorial.

routes.name: Gemini app video
routes.howFromClaude: Claude writes the shot brief; paste it into the Gemini app.
routes.access: Personal accounts need a Google AI plan; Workspace accounts need a qualifying licence; not for users under 18. Uploading video for edits is unavailable in the EEA, Switzerland, the UK and some US states.
routes.cost: Included in the Google AI plan.
routes.notes: Runs Gemini Omni. The fallback when you have no connector, API key or GPU.

routes.name: Google Flow
routes.howFromClaude: Claude writes the shot list; build the scene in Flow.
routes.access: Google account with a qualifying Google AI plan; check Flow's page.
routes.notes: Google's filmmaking workspace. The public page shows little beyond a sign-in, so plan details are unconfirmed.

routes.name: Luma Dream Machine (Ray3.14)
routes.howFromClaude: Claude writes the brief; run it in Dream Machine. A community MCP exists (JochenYang/luma-mcp) but is unofficial.
routes.access: Luma account.
routes.notes: Native 1080p; Modify Video handles clips up to 18 seconds. Ray3.14 does not support character references.

routes.name: Runway app
routes.howFromClaude: Claude writes the brief and the reference plan; run it in Runway.
routes.access: Runway account.
routes.notes: Same models as the Runway MCP route, with the app's editing controls.

routes.name: Midjourney video
routes.howFromClaude: Claude writes the image prompt and motion notes; animate the image in Midjourney.
routes.access: Midjourney subscription.
routes.notes: Animates Midjourney images. Its docs page returned 403 to our checker, so details are unconfirmed.

routes.name: Pika
routes.howFromClaude: Claude writes the brief; run it in Pika.
routes.access: Pika account.
routes.notes: Creator-facing generator focused on short clips and effects.

routes.name: LTX Studio
routes.howFromClaude: Claude writes the script and shot list; build the storyboard in LTX Studio.
routes.access: LTX Studio account.
routes.notes: A production workspace, separate from running the open LTX-Video weights yourself.

routes.name: CapCut and Captions
routes.howFromClaude: Claude writes the cut list, captions and narration script; finish the edit in the app.
routes.access: CapCut or Captions account.
routes.notes: Where most short-form creators finish today. CapCut: capcut.com. No Claude integration is established for either.

routes.name: Wan 2.2, HunyuanVideo, LTX-Video, CogVideoX, Mochi
routes.howFromClaude: Claude Code installs the model or a ComfyUI workflow on a GPU machine and scripts batches. FastVideo and DiffSynth-Studio speed up inference.
routes.access: Open weights, but code licences and weight licences differ. Read each checkpoint's model card: HunyuanVideo, LTX-Video and CogVideoX ship weight licences of their own, and CogVideoX-5B asks commercial users to register.
routes.notes: The realistic-footage route with fixed seeds and no per-second bill. Reruns match only with the same checkpoint, settings and hardware.

routes.name: MoneyPrinterTurbo, explainroo, onetake
routes.howFromClaude: Clone the kit, add your keys, let Claude Code drive its CLI or adapt the templates.
routes.access: Open source; the models they call bill separately.
routes.cost: Whatever LLM, voice and footage providers you plug in.
routes.notes: In zhuyansen/awesome-claude-video-skills' 16-skill test, explainroo finished a film with sound fastest (about two minutes) and onetake held one idea across the cut. Fast output tends toward the default look.

routes.name: Postiz (self-hosted scheduler with MCP)
routes.howFromClaude: Upload the file through the Postiz MCP and stage the post; a human approves before it schedules.
routes.access: Self-hosted Postiz with each platform's OAuth connected.
routes.notes: Posts through each platform's official API rather than browser automation.
